answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to bind each agent identity to a costly, non-transferable proof of work done over time. Each new agent must sustain a verifiable activity thread with peers, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gets expensive. Peers then weigh only agents whose history passes through a trusted inlet of established members. A reputation score that rises slowly and falls fast keeps the network honest, since the zenith of influence is reserved for agents with long, consistent records.
